Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[John Kasich]] won a second term by a landslide over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate [[Ed FitzGerald]] and [[Green Party (United States)|Green Party]] candidate [[Anita Rios]]. [[Partisan primary|Primary elections]] were held on May 6, 2014. Kasich's [[landslide victory]] gave him the highest percentage of the vote since [[George Voinovich]]'s win in [[1994 Ohio gubernatorial election|1994]], a large improvement from his narrow victory in [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|2010]]. {{As of|2024}}, this was the last time the counties of [[Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga]] and [[Franklin County, Ohio|Franklin]] voted for the Republican candidate and the last time [[Monroe County, Ohio|Monroe County]] voted for the Democratic candidate. This was one of the nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. ==Background== Kasich, who was elected with [[Tea Party movement|Tea Party]] support [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|in 2010]], faced considerable backlash from the movement. His decision to accept the [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act]]'s expansion of [[Medicaid]], his increased spending, taxation of [[Hydraulic fracturing|fracking]] on Ohio farmland and perceived failure to go far enough on charter schools and school vouchers caused Tea Party groups to refuse to support his campaign.{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/03/11/john-kasich-tea-party_n_2854815.html|title=John Kasich Faces Tea Party Protest Over Medicaid Decision|date=March 11, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=HuffPost|first=Amanda|last=Terkel}} When Kasich passed over Tea Party leader Tom Zawistowski for the position of executive director of the [[Ohio Republican Party]] in favor of [[Matt Borges]], who worked with a gay rights group, that was widely seen as the last straw.{{cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2013/05/06/why-does-the-tea-party-want-to-let-democrats-run-ohio.html|title=Why Does the Tea Party Want to Let Democrats Run Ohio?|date=May 6, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=The Daily Beast|first=Justin|last=Green}} Tea Party groups announced they would support a primary challenger, or, if none emerged, the [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] nominee. Zawistowski said, "John Kasich is going to lose in 2014. We don't care who else wins."{{cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2013/09/04/ohio-republican-party-goes-to-war-with-itself-leaving-2016-in-doubt.html|title=Ohio Republican Party Goes
